titleEn: I Am Gugu, Just Right as I Am!

pages.text: "I always fall behind." Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, trudged through the snow, panting. Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, looked back from far ahead. Gugu's shoulders sagged.
Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, leaped over the wall. "I wish I were light like Nono and could jump like Kiki," Gugu muttered. The green bag hung low.
Snow suddenly blew hard. Wind rushed into the alley. Nono staggered. Kiki squinted. "I cannot see!" All three stopped.
Grandpa waved beneath the awning. "Children, line up behind Gugu." Gugu went to the front.
Gugu stood with chest out. Behind Gugu, no wind came, and no snow struck. "Not cold back here!" Nono's eyes widened.
Grandpa smiled. "Nono is light and fast. Kiki jumps well. And Gugu?" "Gugu blocks the wind!" Kiki called.
They walked through the storm in a line: Gugu first, Nono next, Kiki last. No one staggered. Gugu puffed the chest out more. "I am Gugu, just right as I am!"
They crunched up to the shop door without getting snow on them. Gugu touched the green bag strap. A warm feeling filled the chest.
Now they called each other, "Fast Nono! Leaping Kiki! Wind-blocking Gugu!" All three laughed.
Grandpa hugged Gugu's shoulders. It is all right to be different from friends. You have something only you can give. Gugu beamed. "I am Gugu, just right as I am!"
